data.name: Mayuransh
data.gender_notes: Mayuransh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mayuransh is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Mayura' which means peacock. In Hindu mythology, the peacock is considered the vehicle of Lord Murugan, also known as Kartikeya, the God of War. The name Mayuransh signifies the power, strength, and grace associated with the peacock and the deity it represents. The name Mayuransh carries the meaning “Peacock Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mayuransh usually hope their child will grow to embody peacock lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodying the virtues of Lord Murugan, this name symbolizes courage, wisdom, and compassion.
data.etymology: Mayuransh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Peacock Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mayuransh total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Mayuransh is a symbol of power, royalty, and auspiciousness in Hindu culture. The name is often given to boys and celebrated as a significant name in Hindu communities. It is also believed that a boy named Mayuransh is blessed with courage, strength, and resilience.
data.spiritual_significance: Mayuransh is a spiritual name that signifies the closest association with Lord Murugan, a powerful Hindu deity. It represents the divine blessings of prosperity, good health, and success in all endeavors. Wearing or chanting the mantra of this name is believed to bring the power and grace of Lord Murugan into one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mayuransh: The name Mayuransh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Mayura' (peacock) and 'Ansh' (essence or soul). It symbolizes the graceful and elegant spirit of the peacock, representing the innate beauty and richness of the soul. This name signifies the individual's connection to the divine, conveying a sense of royalty and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Mayuransh was a Yadav king in ancient India, who is mentioned in the Mahabharata epic. He was a king of Haihayas, a branch of the Yadavas, and ruled over the kingdom of Magadha.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Mahabharata epic, Yadava king, Haihayas, Magadha kingdom

historical_references.reference: Mayuransh was also a name of King Mahendra, the legendary founder of the ancient Shiva temple at Pattadakal, in present-day Karnataka, India. The temple was built around 8th century CE and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Shiva temple, Pattadakal, legendary founder
